| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

golangci-lint run

go test ./...

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

  • Credentials: String, GoString, %v/%+v/%#v/%s (value and pointer) show only Display or [redacted]; Redact handles raw, escaped and decoded forms.
  • Characterization tests: hermetic (noProxyEnvironment), Docker and Podman, 30 cases, green without any production change.

Important (non blocking, fix before step 3 stores a Forward in a struct)

  • internal/netproxy/forward.go:31-33 — Forward keeps raw values in an unexported slice field. fmt does not call String on a value reached through an unexported struct field, so fmt.Sprintf("%+v", someStruct) where someStruct has a field fwd netproxy.Forward prints the raw proxy URL with its password (checked on a minimal reproduction; also %#v). Fix: hold the data behind a pointer (pairs *forwardData, zero value still Empty); fmt then prints an address at depth > 0. Add a test with a struct holding a Forward in an unexported field.

Minor

  • forward.go Redact — a value http://@proxy:3128 (empty user, no password) makes Redact delete every "@" of the text ("me@example.com" becomes "meexample.com"). Skip an empty userinfo.
  • forward.go Redact — an unusable value (e.g. user:pa/ss@proxy:3128) is only redacted as a whole string; its password fragment is not redacted if a tool quotes it partially. Low risk.
  • container_builders_test.go TestContainerBuildersCoverEveryLauncher — checks the table against a literal list in the same file, so it cannot detect a new launcher; its comment claims more. The real guard is step 4: reword the comment.
  • forward_test.go — no test for Redact with two pairs carrying different credentials, nor for the empty-userinfo case above.

input.message:
**Revue DEVDESK-597 (étapes 1 et 2 de DEVDESK-583) : approuvé, aucun point bloquant.** Le commentaire est posté sur DEVDESK-597 avec l'identité reviewer.

**Vérifié**
- `go test` sur `internal/netproxy` et `internal/scan` passe, y compris avec HTTPS_PROXY, http_proxy et NO_PROXY définis dans le parent, avec `-count=2`, et avec `-race` sur netproxy.
- `golangci-lint` donne 0 issue sur les deux paquets, `gofmt` est propre, `GOOS=windows go vet` est OK. Aucun fichier du dépôt modifié ; mes essais sont dans le scratchpad.

**Lecture**
- La majuscule passe avant la minuscule, une valeur vide compte comme non définie, et les deux casings reçoivent la même valeur.
- ALL_PROXY et FTP_PROXY sont ignorées.
- La lecture est unique (`sync.OnceValue`). Le test en sous-processus a une lecture de contrôle et un `runChild` qui retire les variables de proxy de la machine.

**Refactor de `describe.go`**
- C'est une extraction pure (`firstNonEmpty`, `parseProxyValue`), sans changement de comportement. Les tests existants restent verts.

**Fuite d'identifiants**
- `String`, `GoString` et `%v/%+v/%#v/%s`, en valeur et en pointeur, ne montrent que `Display` ou `[redacted]`.
- `Redact` couvre les formes brute, échappée et décodée. Il épargne les mots de passe courts hors de la valeur complète.

**Tests de caractérisation**
- Ils sont hermétiques (`noProxyEnvironment`), couvrent Docker et Podman, et passent sans aucun changement de production. L'étape 2 est conforme.

**Important, non bloquant (à corriger avant que l'étape 3 range un `Forward` dans une struct)**
- `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/feat/devdesk-583-container-proxy/internal/netproxy/forward.go:31-33` : `Forward` garde les valeurs brutes dans un champ non exporté. Je l'ai reproduit avec un exemple minimal : `fmt` n'appelle pas `String` sur une valeur atteinte par un champ non exporté. `fmt.Sprintf("%+v", s)` ou `%#v`, avec `s` une struct qui a un champ `fwd netproxy.Forward`, affiche donc l'URL brute avec son mot de passe.
- Correction suggérée : mettre les données derrière un pointeur (`pairs *forwardData`, le zéro restant `Empty`), car `fmt` n'affiche alors qu'une adresse. Ajouter un test avec une struct qui contient un `Forward` en champ non exporté.

**Mineurs**
- `Redact` avec `http://@proxy:3128` (user vide, sans mot de passe) supprime tous les "@" du texte : "me@example.com" devient "meexample.com". Il faut ignorer un userinfo vide.
- Pour une valeur inutilisable comme `user:pa/ss@proxy:3128`, `Redact` ne remplace que la chaîne entière. Un fragment du mot de passe cité par un outil resterait visible. Risque faible.
- `internal/scan/container_builders_test.go`, `TestContainerBuildersCoverEveryLauncher` : le test compare la table à une liste littérale du même fichier, donc il ne détecte aucun nouveau lanceur. Son commentaire en promet plus. Le vrai garde est celui de l'étape 4, à citer dans le commentaire.
- Il manque des tests de `Redact` avec deux paires aux identifiants différents, et avec un userinfo vide.
